questions.question: What is true about doubles and triples?

options.text: They can turn more easily than other vehicles.
They should be driven 20 mph below the speed limit.
The driver must spot dangers far ahead.
They should not be driven in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver must spot dangers far ahead.
questions.explanation: Doubles and triples can roll over or jackknife if driven roughly. Drivers must look far ahead to see hazards early. This gives them time to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What is the purpose of tie-downs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop cargo from moving.
questions.explanation: Tie-downs keep cargo from shifting or falling off flatbed trailers and open trailers. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: If tailgated, increase the space in front of your vehicle. This helps you avoid sudden stops that could cause a crash. It also makes it easier for the other driver to pass. Speeding up only makes things more dangerous.

questions.question: Where can retreaded tires be used on a bus?
questions.correctAnswerText: The rear of the bus.
questions.explanation: Retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rollovers?

options.text: Keep the load at the back of the trailer.
Keep the load on one side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly around turns.
questions.explanation: To prevent rollovers, load cargo as low as possible. Also take curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: What happens if the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) breaks?

options.text: A yellow light turns on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow light turns on the dashboard.
questions.explanation: When ABS fails, a yellow warning light shows on the instrument panel to alert you.

questions.question: What should you do if the low air pressure light comes on while driving?

options.text: You can only brake if there is enough air in the tanks.
You can brake 14 times before the air runs out.
Continue driving normally and check the brakes later.
Keep driving but turn on your flashers to warn others.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only brake if there is enough air in the tanks.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure light turns on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. You can only brake as long as there is enough air left in the tanks.

questions.question: What should you do when carrying a wide load?

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules.
Honk at other drivers to make them move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules.
questions.explanation: Wide, long, or overweight loads need special permits. They may also have driving restrictions.

questions.question: What should you do if you must drive very slowly?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, warn drivers behind you by turning on your emergency flashers, if local law allows.

questions.question: Why are roads very slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel washes to the middle of the lane.
Tires are not made for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil and grease on the road, making a slick film. As rain continues, this mixture eventually washes away.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT something motorists should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people who are not paying attention to traffic. Watch out for road workers, drivers talking to passengers, and children near the road.

questions.question: When checking your mirrors, you should:

options.text: Not use the passenger side mirror.
Not use the driver's side mirror.
Look in each mirror for a long time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both mirrors.
questions.explanation: To drive safely, you need to know what is happening on all sides of your vehicle. Check both mirrors often while driving.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver on the road, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay far away from them.
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, keep a safe distance. Be very careful if you pass them because they may not see you and could drift into your lane.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when rain first starts because:

options.text: Rain mixes with oil on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain first starts. The rain mixes with oil and grease on the road, creating a slippery film. As more rain falls, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: If a trailer is not at the correct height when connecting it:

options.text: The connection will be more secure.

questions.correctAnswerText: The connection may fail.
questions.explanation: Before connecting a tractor and trailer, make sure the trailer is at the correct height. If it is too low, the trailer may be damaged. If it is too high, it may not connect properly.

questions.question: According to the National Sleep Foundation, about ____ of people have driven while feeling sleepy.
questions.correctAnswerText: 60 percent
questions.explanation: The National Sleep Foundation found that 60 percent of Americans have driven while sleepy. 36 percent have actually fallen asleep while driving.

questions.question: Air brakes are:

options.text: A good way to stop large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good way to stop large vehicles.
questions.explanation: When properly maintained, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol level?

options.text: How hot or cold the drinks were

questions.correctAnswerText: How hot or cold the drinks were
questions.explanation: Three things affect blood alcohol level: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and the person's weight.

questions.question: To leave a parking space as safely as possible, you should park:

options.text: So you must back up to leave.
So you can drive forward to leave.
On the side of a road, not in a lot.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can drive forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous. Whenever possible, park where you can drive forward to exit.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, you use the parking brake by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pulling a diamond-shaped yellow knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a diamond-shaped yellow knob. Pull it out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.
